response.content:
For a head-on collision, the center-of-mass energy satisfies

\[
s=4E_\gamma \epsilon_{\rm CMB}.
\]

Pair production requires \(\sqrt{s}\ge 2m_e c^2\), so

\[
4E_\gamma \epsilon_{\rm CMB}\ge 4m_e^2
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
E_\gamma \ge \frac{m_e^2}{\epsilon_{\rm CMB}}.
\]

Using \(m_e=0.511\,{\rm MeV}=5.11\times10^5\,{\rm eV}\) and \(\epsilon_{\rm CMB}=10^{-3}\,{\rm eV}\):

\[
E_\gamma \ge \frac{(5.11\times10^5)^2}{10^{-3}}
\simeq 2.6\times10^{14}\,{\rm eV}
=2.6\times10^5\,{\rm GeV}.
\]

So gamma rays above about this energy have their propagation limited by \(\gamma\gamma\to e^+e^-\) on the CMB.

Answer: B
